messages.author: c93b61679b5dd671
messages.subject: Re: About length_thresh
parts:
Hi Tao,

Yes the default threshold is set fairly arbitrarily. Also it is the lower bound that usually matters -- we want to filter out small exonic targets that aren't efficiently captured.

I pushed some updates in GitHub for CODEX. Please use the code below to update your CODEX package.

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_github("yuchaojiang/CODEX/package")

Let me know if you have further questions. I am cc'ing our Google user group in case other users have similar questions.

Cheers,
Yuchao

Sent from my iPhone

On Apr 26, 2016, at 7:18 PM, Tao, Shu <sh...@coh.org> wrote:

Hi Yuchao,

 

 

This is Shu Tao from City of Hope National Medical Center. Thank you very much for developing CODEX such a useful tool for CNV identification. I do have a question on the length_thresh (exons that extremely short or long): 20-2000. I am wondering if the recommended upper limit (2000) would be too small for human exon.

 

I look forward to your reply at your earliest convenience. Thank you!

 

 

 

Shu

messages.subject: RE: About length_thresh
parts:
Hi Tao,

The number of latent factors cannot exceed the number of normal samples if you use the normalize2() function. It’s similar to the fact that the number of PCs cannot exceed the matrix dimension in PCA.

Hope this clarifies,

Yuchao
